Source: A 71-year-old man arrives to the emergency room appearing cyanotic and having weak, shallow respirations.
An arterial blood gas is drawn with results as shown below: This morning, he experienced poor grip strength and progressive difficulty breathing.
His temperature is 99.0°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg, pulse is 92/min, and respirations are 28/min with an oxygen saturation of 86% O2 on room air.
He is brought in by his home care nurse, who reports that the patient has a history of myasthenia gravis and frequent urinary tract infections.
The patient’s medications include pyridostigmine and aspirin, both of which he takes as prescribed.
He was receiving gentamicin infusions for his infections.
